summary: Dell XPS fleet: BIOS fan-curve locked after 16.2.8 update, blocking thermal calibration during provisioning
description:
Issue summary: After rolling BIOS 16.2.8 to a batch of Dell XPS developer laptops, devices consistently start with the fan-curve set to 'locked' state during provisioning. Thermal calibration step in our imaging workflow reports 'fan profile unmodifiable' and the node is marked failed.

Impact: Blocks provisioning of a subset (~18%) of new/returned XPS laptops in the prod-us-west staging fleet. Affected devices throttle under load because calibration cannot adjust fan curves; delays onboarding and increases repair queue.

Observed behavior: Fresh devices or devices returning from depot with BIOS 16.2.8 applied show the same behavior. Fan control still responds to ACPI calls (fans spin) but the firmware rejects profile writes from our calibration utility (exit code 5). Event logs show BIOS message: 'FAN_CURVE_LOCK: vendor lock enabled'. Older BIOS versions (<=16.1.4) do not show the lock.

Hypothesis: Dell OEM firmware introduced a new secure fan-curve lock flag in 16.2.8 that prevents vendor tools from writing calibration profiles unless an OEM signed token is present. Our calibration utility (support-scripts/fancal) uses standard WMI/ACPI calls that used to work. The firmware change may have been rolled out silently with 16.2.8.

Temporary impact mitigation: Manual workaround available at depot: use Dell Diagnostics > thermal override to apply a temporary profile. Not scalable for fleet onboarding.

Next steps requested: Eng (firmware/bios) to confirm whether flag is intentional and whether a signed token or vendor handshake is required. Provisioning team to adjust imaging workflow to detect locked fans and route to repair queue automatically. Hardware team to identify affected serial ranges sent to partners in last 30 days.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start with a Dell XPS 15/17 with BIOS 16.2.8 installed (factory or updated)
2) Boot into provisioning image (PXE->WinPE->imaging task sequence) and run support-scripts/fancal --stage=calibrate
3) Observe fancal exit with code 5 and log entry: 'FAN_CURVE_LOCK: write access denied'
4) Check Windows Event Log: Application > FANCAL > Error 0x05; check BIOS serial log via vendor log collector for fan state
5) Reflash to 16.1.4 (rollback) and repeat; calibration succeeds and device completes provisioning.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09 09:14 - Intake: Support received first report from depot (site: SEA-depot-3) after 6 failures in a single imaging batch.
2026-03-09 10:02 - Reproduced in lab on 3/3 devices with 16.2.8; rollback to 16.1.4 fixes. Captured bios debug region via fwtool (attached to artifact bucket).
2026-03-10 14:33 - Eng hypothesis: OEM added a signed lock bit. Reached out to Dell partner rep; case #SR-992183 opened. Requested firmware release notes and whitelist process.
2026-03-11 11:47 - Provisioning team updated imaging pipeline to detect fancal exit code and tag device for manual handling. Reduced batch failure rate to 2% (edge cases where rollback not possible).
2026-03-12 16:20 - Hardware identified serial number pattern S/N prefix "DXP-00C" present in 60% of failures; forwarded to Dell SR to prioritize investigation.
workarounds: 1) Depot manual: Use Dell Diagnostics thermal override to set a temporary curve so imaging can complete.
2) Rolling back BIOS to 16.1.4 allows our calibration utility to succeed (applies to devices where rollback is permitted).
3) Imaging pipeline change: Detect fancal exit and auto-move device to 'requires-firmware-review' queue to avoid repeated failures.

next_actions: 1) Firmware Eng: Coordinate with Dell SR-992183 to confirm whether 16.2.8 intentionally introduces fan-curve lock and request guidance or signed utility (ETA requested by 2026-03-17).
2) Hardware/Depot: Start targeted rollback campaign for affected serial ranges where rollback is allowed and time-efficient.
3) Provisioning: Keep imaging pipeline detection in place and update runbooks; escalate if failure rate increases above 5% in next 7 days.
4) Support: Prepare internal communication to on-call depot techs with temporary manual override steps and safety precautions.
